# The Fine Line

Your art portfolio site — plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build tools required.

## Pages

- `index.html` — home page with hero + featured work
- `gallery.html` — the full gallery
- `about.html` — bio and contact details

## Adding or replacing artwork

You never need to touch the HTML to add new art. Everything the gallery shows comes from one file:

`assets/js/gallery-data.js`

1. Drop your image file into `assets/images/` (jpg, png, or webp all work).
2. Open `assets/js/gallery-data.js` and copy one of the existing entries, e.g.:
   ```js
   {
     title: "Your Piece Title",
     category: "Illustration",
     image: "assets/images/your-file.jpg",
     description: "A line or two about the piece.",
     featured: true
   },
   ```
3. Set `featured: true` if you also want it to show on the home page; `false` keeps it in the gallery only.
4. Save the file. That's it — both `index.html` and `gallery.html` read from this same list.

Update the placeholder text and email/social links in `about.html` whenever you're ready.

## Going live on GitHub Pages

1. Push this branch, then merge it into `main` (or open the PR and merge it) so `main` has these files.
2. In the GitHub repo, go to **Settings → Pages**.
3. Under **Build and deployment**, set **Source** to "Deploy from a branch", pick `main` and `/ (root)`, then **Save**.
4. GitHub will publish the site at `https://<your-username>.github.io/<repo-name>/` within a minute or two.

## Wrapping your own domain around it

Once Pages is live:

1. Still in **Settings → Pages**, under **Custom domain**, enter your domain (e.g. `thefineline.com` or `www.thefineline.com`) and save. GitHub will create a `CNAME` file in the repo automatically.
2. At your domain registrar (wherever you bought the domain), add DNS records pointing to GitHub:
   - For an apex domain (`thefineline.com`), add **A records** pointing to:
     ```
     185.199.108.153
     185.199.109.153
     185.199.110.153
     185.199.111.153
     ```
   - For a `www` subdomain, add a **CNAME record** pointing to `<your-username>.github.io`.
3. Back in **Settings → Pages**, once DNS has propagated (can take up to a few hours), tick **Enforce HTTPS**.

Tell me your exact domain name and I can add the `CNAME` file and double-check the DNS records for you directly.

## Once your domain is live

Each page has `og:image` tags (used for link previews on social media, iMessage, Discord, etc.) that currently point to a relative image path. Once your domain is wrapped, tell me the URL and I'll update those to full `https://yourdomain.com/...` links so previews render correctly everywhere.

Acts One to Five & Epilogue
BMF:MD Trilogy — Part II
Written by
Hamish Newland
Final draft — 14 October 2026
Grey Filter / The Fine Line BMF: 3K | Complete Screenplay | Final draft
CONTENTS
ACT ONE — THE SCAN ..................................... 1
ACT TWO — THE BIG ONE ................................. 13

ACT ONE
THE SCAN
INT. SUBURBAN GARAGE — LATE AFTERNOON (1971)
A car up on blocks. A pair of legs sticks out from
underneath it — work boots, oil-dark overalls. A radio on
the bench plays something thin and tinny. Beside it, a
worn black Bible, spine cracked. High on the back wall, a
shotgun rests on two pegs, out of the light. Dust hangs in
the slant of light from the open door.
THE BOY (10) sits cross-legged on the concrete. In front
of him: a small styrofoam figure — one of the 3K heroes —
and an open tin of paint. He works slowly. Tongue between
his teeth. Careful.
He asks it without looking up.
THE BOY
Dad. Are demons real?
Under the car, the wrench stops.
His FATHER doesn't slide out.
FATHER (O.S.)
They're real.
A long beat. Long enough that the Boy looks over at the
boots.
FATHER (O.S.) (CONT'D)
But they're in your head. And they
only have the teeth you give them.
The Boy nods, like he's been handed a fact. He goes back
to the paint.
The wrench starts up again.
PUSH IN on the Boy's eye. Closer. Closer. HOLD on it.
MATCH CUT TO:
INT. PHONE BOOTH — NIGHT (1995)
An eye — DAVE's. Pull back.
DAVE (40s) stands in a phone booth, the receiver still on
its hook. Just standing. Gathering himself. His hands are 2.
BMF: 3K | Complete Screenplay | Final draft
shaking.
He lifts the receiver. Dials. Talks low — we don't need
the words.
Over his shoulder, through the glass: a car rolls in
across the road and stops. Headlights stay on. In the
driver's seat, a strange YELLOW SILHOUETTE — too vague to
make out.
The headlights flood the booth. Dave turns, squints into
them. Turns back. Keeps talking.
EXT. STREET — CONTINUOUS
From behind: a huge hand rests on the car window frame.
THE MANAGER steps out and stands by the open door. We
never see his face.
THE 3K OVERLAY clunks in.
It doesn't fade up — it assembles. Blocky, mechanical,
analogue, pieces clicking into place. It finds Dave
through the glass and drives in on his hand.
A crude 1950s-style X-RAY. Bones. The tremor. HOLD on it —
let the audience read it as data.
This is how the Manager sees the world. Not a gadget and
not a vision: a filter he built as a boy and has never
switched off. Where we see a person, he sees a system —
readouts, meters, measurements, things to be read,
managed, and kept in range. Only we see it. No one in the
story ever does.
Clunk. The overlay drops out.
INT./EXT. PHONE BOOTH — CONTINUOUS
Dave hangs up. Sighs. Something sad in it.
He steps out of the booth and lights a cigarette. Draws
deep.
Across the road, the Manager stands. Watching.
THE OVERLAY again. Same angle, same clunking arrival. In
on the hand.
The bones are still. 3.

At the top of the frame, a METER climbs — 75%. It stops
short.
Clunk out.
Back on Dave. The hair on the back of his neck lifts.
Goosebumps.
He turns — and looks straight at the Manager.
They hold each other's eyes across the road.
Then the Manager moves. We only get it as Dave sees it: a
blur in the distance — and then a man standing there.
THE SHOT. The two of them, square on, across the road from
each other. The size difference is startling.
The Manager walks right up to him. Takes out a pack of
cigarettes. Taps the base with one finger.
Two cigarettes pop up.
Dave takes both.
The Manager doesn't react. At all.
A nod. Dave nods back.
The Manager turns and walks away.
TITLE SEQUENCE
EXT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — NIGHT
A tall, dark house on an ordinary suburban street. The
Manager's car pulls in. He gets out.
On the veranda, MIKEY (50s), small and wiry, sits with a
CAT in his lap. He sees the Manager, sets the cat down,
stands to rigid attention and throws a salute. Deadpan.
Taking the piss.
The Manager returns the salute. Properly. No smile.
Mikey sits back down and goes on petting the cat.
He reaches for a cigarette. The lighter slips out of his
left hand and rolls off the boards. He picks it up with
his right and shakes the left out, like it has gone to
sleep. Shrugs. Lights up. 4.

INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — LIVING ROOM — NIGHT
SID (20s) and TAMARA (20s) on the floor, a glass pipe
passing between them. Music playing. Nothing urgent.
They're just here.
The front door. The Manager comes in.
Sid and Tamara scramble up to attention, mock-formal. The
Manager returns it, unreadable behind the mask, and keeps
walking.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — KITCHEN — CONTINUOUS
He washes his hands. Properly — to the wrist. Dries them.
Ties on an apron. Pulls on an oven mitt.
He takes a crock pot out of the oven and begins to serve.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — LIVING ROOM — CONTINUOUS
TAMARA
Two hundred.
(beat)
Doesn't sound like much when you say
it.
SID
It's not much.
TAMARA
Then why haven't we got it?
SID
We'll have it. We're sorted. Relax.
Neither of them believes it. Then the song does something
they both love and they let it go, heads nodding.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — DINING ROOM — LATER
The Manager sets a pot of STEW on the table, still in his
apron. Steam rolls off it.
Mikey wanders in and sits. On the way past, he reaches up
— he has to reach — and slings an arm around the Manager's
shoulders. Two pats. 5.

MIKEY
Beautiful, mate.
They eat. It's warm. It's genuinely nice.
The Manager doesn't sit. He never eats with them. He turns
and walks out.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — HALLWAY — CONTINUOUS
He walks to a door at the end of the hall. The one only he
goes through.
On the wall beside it hangs a small wooden CRUCIFIX,
dusty, the only thing on those walls. He doesn't look at
it.
He flicks off the apron. Strips the mitt from one hand —
the other stays free for the door handle.
Latex gloves. A lab coat.
He opens the door and pushes through a curtain of plastic
strips — the supermarket kind. They slap shut behind him.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — DINING ROOM — CONTINUOUS
Sid, Tamara and Mikey, bowls nearly empty, laughing.
TAMARA
He salutes back. Every time.
MIKEY
You started it.
TAMARA
This whole thing is insane.
SID
Is it though?
(counting on his fingers)
We owe two hundred. Nobody touches us

easy.
He opens his hands: what's the problem?
Mikey shrugs. Not for it, not against it.
MIKEY
It's a lot, is what it is.
He tears a bit of bread and mops his bowl. 6.

INT. THE MANAGER'S ROOM — NIGHT
Clinical. Clean. Scales. Baggies in neat rows. A single
lamp.
THE LEDGER sits in the centre of the desk. He opens it the
way you'd open a Bible.
Page after page of meticulous handwriting. Columns for
everything: ROOM TEMPERATURE. MEALS. ENERGY. SLEEP.
SUBSTANCE GIVEN. SUBSTANCE DUE.
Under SID, an extra column: ALCOHOL — type, percentage,
volume.
THE OVERLAY clunks in over the page. Whatever he looks at,
it turns into numbers. It is how he keeps the world under
control.
The ink lifts. The ledger's data downloads up into the
grid — chunking, sorting, sliding into a crude FILING
CABINET component that clicks shut.
The overlay shifts. A horizontal meter builds itself for
each of them: a narrow GREEN BAND in the middle. Too much,
and they drift off. Too little, and they don't come back.
The Manager weighs out crystal. Taps the scale. Adds a
grain. Takes one away.
Into a baggie. Perfect.
One for Tamara — exactly enough to sit her in the green.
Sid's is different. The overlay pulls his alcohol from the
filing cabinet and nudges the numbers. The Manager
adjusts.
Two baggies. Labelled. Lined up.
INT. DAVE'S HOUSE — DAY
The next day. Dave opens his front door onto nothing.
Bare boards. Bare walls. No furniture anywhere. A house
bought and never started.
In the corner of one room: a mattress on the floor, a
sleeping bag on top. That's it. 7.

INT. DAVE'S HOUSE — PANTRY — CONTINUOUS
He takes out a bag of bread gone green and furred. Looks
at it. Drops it in the bin.
A packet of water crackers instead. He eats a couple
standing up. Chews. Gives up.
DAVE
Fuck this.
(grabbing his coat)
Coffee.
He's out the door.
INT. THE GOTHIC HOUSE — LIVING ROOM — NIGHT
A MAP spread across the table. The Manager walks Sid and
Tamara through it: the route, the timings, the drill.
Again. And again.
He puts on one of his custom MASKS — a small antenna at
the crown. Clicks a walkie. Static. Good.
He sets out two metal buckets.
Stops.
Takes down a third. Says nothing about it.
He stacks all three and hands them to Sid.
Sid looks at the stack. Looks at the Manager. Doesn't ask.
EXT. SUBURBAN STREET — NIGHT
Dave walks, coffee gone, cigarette lit. He stops by a
BLOKE sitting out front of a shop, bums a light, and falls
into easy nothing-talk.
Then Dave looks up — and his face goes slack with absolute
perplexity.
EXT. SUPERMARKET — NIGHT — DAVE'S POV
In the distance: Sid and Tamara edging round the corner of
the supermarket like they're clearing a building. Flat to
the wall. Hand signals. Buckets. 8.

Above them, on a grassy rise — the Manager, in the antenna
mask, directing them with sharp hand gestures.
EXT. SUBURBAN STREET — CONTINUOUS
Dave can't believe it.
DAVE
(under his breath)
That's him.
He stares at the Manager. Just stares.

The back of the Manager's neck. The hair lifts.
Goosebumps.
He turns — and finds Dave already looking at him.

Evening.

...Mum?

So who's the big fella? I've seen him

Mate — sorry. We've just gotta get

Okay.

# BMF TRILOGY: CANON LAW & DESIGN MANUAL
## Single Source of Truth (SSOT) — Version 1.1

---

## SECTION I: THE TRILOGY ARCHITECTURE

The BMF Trilogy traces the systematic, generational transition of psychological coping mechanisms: moving from Religious Mania to Digital Delusion, and finally to Predatory Realism.

```
[BMF C1V1: GENESIS]       ──>       [BMF 3000: ORIGINAL]       ──>        [BMF Y2K: SEQUEL]
   (The Father)                        (The Manager)                       (The Adult)

HIGH-MAINTENANCE PROPHECY              DEFENSIVE DELUSION                  PREDATORY REALISM
  Sobriety is failure.              The 1995 HUD is safety.              The HUD is shattered.
 "I am the Holy Spirit."               "I am saving them."               "I am the predator."
```

### Era Comparison Matrix

| Pillar | BMF C1V1 (Prequel) | BMF 3000 (Original) | BMF Y2K (Sequel) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Era / Timeline** | Late 1960s – Early 1970s | 1995 (The Cold Summer) | 1999 – NYE 2000 Transition |
| **Perspective** | The Father (The Pastor) | The Manager (The Son) | The Manager (Hardened Adult) |
| **Primary Verb** | **Perform** (Ledger, Preaching) | **Exploit** (Dosing, Crew Runs) | **Observe** (Stealth, Tracking) |
| **Primary Space** | Church Pulpit, Sedan, Garage | Supermarket Lot, Gothic House | State Penitentiary Yard, Cells |
| **Core Conflict** | Crisis of Faith, Self-Destruction | Escaping Reality via HUD Delusion | Surviving Prison via Yard Power |
| **Resource Gate** | Church Ledger (Tithe Skimming) | Vices (Cigar, Booze, Weed, Gear) | Leverage, Black Market Favors |
| **Visual Theme** | Analog, "Felony-Religious", Ink | 1995 Grime masked by Neon HUD | Cold, Monochrome CRT, Surveillance |

---

## SECTION II: BMF C1V1 — GENESIS (THE PREQUEL)

### 1. Core Philosophy: The Holy High-Wire Act

Unlike BMF 3000, you are **not managing other people**. You are managing your own accelerating self-destruction.

* **The Sincere Deception:** The Father is not a cheap con artist. He is an authentic fanatic. He believes the "Holy Spirit" speaks to him directly through his high.
* **The "Not-a-Junkie" Rule:** In his mind, drug use is a heavy, sacred burden — a sacrificial "anointing" required to tune into God's channel. Taking money from the church ledger is not stealing; it is a divine reallocation to keep the Lord's vessel functional.
* **The "Wane" Mechanic:** Sobriety is mechanical death. As the chemical high decays, the gameplay interface degrades — unsteadiness increases, options grey out, tasks stutter, and deacons notice your tremors (raising Heat).

### 2. Core Gameplay Loop

```
[1. THE AUDIT]  ──>  [2. THE DOSE]  ──>  [3. THE ERRAND]  ──>  [4. THE HARVEST]
 (Skim Ledger)       (Acquire High)       (Sustaining Mask)      (Supermarket Preach)
```

1. **The Audit:** Access the physical church accounting ledger. Skim money within the "Goldilocks Zone" (too little and you withdraw; too much and you trigger Deacon suspicion/audits).
2. **The Dose:** Ingest the supply to balance your "Divine Clarity" state. If you hit the sweet spot, the UI becomes clear, and actions streamline.
3. **The Errand:** Execute daily church chores (cleaning the garage, visiting sick parishioners, prep work) to suppress suspicion (Heat).
4. **The Harvest (Supermarket Preaching):** Stand on a crate outside the sodium-lit grocery store. Deliver charismatic, volatile sermons to extract maximum change ($20 target) from the shoppers.

### 3. Visuals & Feel: Submerged Surrealism

* **Restrained Surrealism:** Avoid generic fantasy designs. The surreal elements are purely optical illusions, visual shifts, and audio distortions reflecting the Father's deteriorating chemical mind (e.g., parking lot lights shifting into a holy choir, numbers in the ledger briefly shimmering before stabilizing).
* **The UI:** Designed to look like a coffee-stained 1960s desk ledger with rough handwritten amendments, typewritten court records, and strange religious symbols hand-drawn in the margins.

# BMF:3K — Interactive Pitch Roadmap

**Current structural roadmap · Data and navigation planning only**

> **Status:** Structure in progress · Artwork and final page copy to be added later

## 1. Roadmap Purpose

This document defines the intended end state of the BMF:3K interactive pitch before artwork, screenshots, final visual assets, and detailed page copy are added.

It is the current planning anchor for:

- page order
- spatial navigation
- page roles

This roadmap does **not** lock final artwork, final typography, final prose, or unresolved narrative decisions.

## 2. End-State Experience

The audience enters through a one-time 3K Overlay launch sequence and then arrives at the centre landing page.

From the centre, the pitch is explored as a horizontal sequence of five connected pages:

```text
[FAR LEFT]              [NEAR LEFT]              [CENTRE]              [NEAR RIGHT]              [FAR RIGHT]
ACT CONCEPT      ←      TONE / ART       ←      HERO PAGE      →      BMF:3K DOCS       →      TRILOGY TEASERS
Scrollable Act I       Artwork and              Main cover art         Narrative and             C1:V1 + Y2K
concept in full         visual reference        Brief premise          document files           brief teasers
```

The centre page is the anchor. The pages to either side are not separate unrelated sections; they are stations in one navigable pitch file.

## 3. Core Navigation Model

### 3.1 Primary axis

The main navigation is horizontal and spatial.

- The user can move left or right from the centre.
- The centre page is the main return point.
- The user can move one station at a time.
- Directional controls remain available at the edges of the experience.
- Keyboard left and right controls should mirror the visual navigation.
- Touch users should be able to swipe between pages without losing page hierarchy.

### 3.2 Page positions

1. where they are
2. how far they are from the centre

4. what exists to the right

The navigation should be integrated into the operational-file frame rather than presented as a generic website menu.

## 4. Launch Sequence

### 4.1 Purpose

The launch sequence introduces the 3K Overlay as the operating environment of the pitch.

It is an opening event, not a page users repeatedly revisit.

### 4.2 Behaviour

- Plays once on app launch.
- Lasts at least 6 seconds.
- Must not exceed 9 seconds before access is available.
- Builds the 3K Overlay through line construction and monitor-scan behaviour.
- Resolves to the prompt `> MANAGE DECLINE_`.
- Opens directly into the centre Hero / Landing page.
- Does not replay when navigating between the five pages.
- Does not replay when returning to the centre.

### 4.3 Launch state sequence

| Phase | Intended function |
|---|---|
| Void | Establishes a blank, controlled starting field |
| Overlay construction | Builds the lime structural grid |
| Diagnostic pass | Introduces the magenta trace language |
| Monitor scan | Reveals the title and supporting status information |
| Prompt resolve | Presents `> MANAGE DECLINE_` |
| Access | Opens the centre Hero / Landing page |

### 4.4 Launch access rule

The prompt becomes actionable after the 6-second minimum. The hard maximum access boundary is 9 seconds.

The user should be able to enter through:

- click
- tap
- keyboard Enter

## 5. Persistent 3K Overlay

After launch, the Overlay nests into the pitch shell and remains present across all five pages.

It is the shared visual and navigational frame, not a separate destination.

### 5.1 Global behaviour

- Always visible in some form.
- Strongest on launch and the centre Hero page.
- More restrained on the Tone / Art, Act Concept, Documents, and Trilogy pages.
- Makes minor positional, geometric, or registration changes on each page.
- Never overwhelms readable documents.
- Never becomes a literal sci-fi HUD.

### 5.2 Intensity plan

| Page | Overlay treatment |
|---|---|
| Launch | Full construction, scan, and diagnostic behaviour |
| Hero / Landing | Strongest resolved Overlay field and frame |
| Tone / Art | Present as framing, registration, and image-surface marks |
| Act Concept | Reduced field activity so the long scrollable concept remains readable |
| Documents | Quiet frame, restrained rules, minimal background movement |
| Trilogy Teasers | Controlled reference marks and a slight page-specific shift |

### 5.3 Shared frame components

The shell may contain:

- top and bottom structural rules
- corner brackets
- page reference markers
- left and right directional indicators
- position labels such as `-2 / -1 / 0 / +1 / +2`
- small scan or registration ticks
- active page title

These components are structural and should remain consistent as page content changes.

## 1. WHAT THIS GAME IS

**Bum A Fag - 3000AD** is a darkly satirical, narratively-rich resource-management / career-simulator.

### The Core Conceit
The player thinks they're a "Shift Manager" running a futuristic operation from 3000AD, commanding "operatives" in a "Grand Court Center." They're not. It's **actually 1996**, and they're a homeless man in a gas station parking lot, hallucinating. The "operatives" are other homeless people. The "resources" are cigarettes, booze, weed, and crystal. The holographic UI is the player's delusion — and it cracks over time as the game escalates.

### Branding
- Title: **"BUM A FAG - 3000"** (previously called "Manager of Decline")
- Hub HUD: `BAF3K`
- Legal entity: `BAF3K HOLDINGS PTY LTD`
- Dossier stamp: `CLASSIFIED - BAF3K PERSONNEL`

  → day_end → hub (next day)

### 3.2 The 4 Hub Stations

3. **Operations Board** — Expeditions + Main Missions + Ascension trigger

### 3.3 Mission Tiers
- **Expeditions**: Short, repeatable, resource-gathering runs with resource buy-in. Grid exploration. Tier-gated.
- **Main Missions** (4 total — the narrative backbone):
  1. **THE INITIATION** — First real job. Unlocks Tier 2 expeditions.
  2. **THE TERRITORY WAR** — Crew loyalty tested. Unlocks new NPC flows.
  3. **THE SYNDICATE HANDSHAKE** — Big leagues. Permanent consequences. Unlocks Tier 3.
  4. **THE ASCENSION / EXIT** — Endgame. Multiple endings based on philosophy + stats.

### 3.4 Resources (max 30 each, server-enforced)

- **Alcohol** (medium)
- **Weed** (uncommon)
- **Crystals** (rare — required for Main Missions)

## 4. RPG SYSTEMS

### 4.1 Player Stats (10 points allocated at creation)
- **NERVE** (default 2) — heat management, conflict escape
- **SILVER TONGUE** (default 3) — recruitment, affinity, dialogue
- **CONSTITUTION** (default 3) — NPC tolerance buffer
- **SCAVENGER** (default 2) — expedition yield, loot bonuses

### 4.2 Philosophy (choose one at creation)
| Philosophy | Accent Color | Vibe | Bonus |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SHEPHERD** | `#00FFFF` cyan | "I look after my people." | +20% CONSTITUTION, +10% SILVER TONGUE |
| **ENTREPRENEUR** | `#CCAA00` gold | "This is just business." | +20% SCAVENGER, +10% NERVE |
| **PROPHET** | `#BF00FF` violet | "They will follow." | +20% NERVE, +10% SILVER TONGUE. Faster shrine growth. More intense hallucinations. |

Philosophy shapes the delusion's manifestation: SHEPHERD sees the gas station as a shelter, ENTREPRENEUR as a franchise, PROPHET as a church.

### 4.3 Escalation System (`lib/escalation.ts`)
Level 0–10, calculated from recruited NPCs + tolerance + expeditions + heat + day.

Phases: `clean → cracking → sweating → bleeding → broken`

Visual escalation: flicker intensity increases, sweat/moisture layers appear, reality bleeds through portraits, neon becomes erratic, shrine grows from "Notes & Clippings" → "THE WALL OF PROVIDENCE". Player title evolves from "Shift Manager" → "Regional Director" → "THE ETERNAL ONE."

### 4.4 The Flicker / Reality System
As Main Missions are completed, reality breaks through harder:
- Mission 1 done: brief static cuts (0.5s)
- Mission 2 done: full scene swaps (2–3s), NPC names momentarily change
- Mission 3 done: sustained reality bleeds (5–10s), fluorescent lights stay on, gas pump sounds audible
- Mission 4: full reveal — delusion shatters or solidifies (philosophy-dependent)

## 5. CONSEQUENCE LOOP (Heat System)

- **Heat 0–4**: Normal ops.
- **Heat 5–6**: Warning notification at day-end.
- **Heat 7–8**: Critical warning + RAID RISK (pseudo-random roll at day-end).
- **Heat 9+**: Failed raid → game over.
- **Heat 10+**: Immediate game over.

### Raid Event
- Triggered when heat ≥ 7 at day-end.
- API: `/api/game/raid` — confiscates 30–60% of resources, drops heat to 40%.
- 3-phase cinematic (intro → damage report → result), ~8s.

### Game Over / Ascension
- Game over has philosophy-appropriate ending text + final stats + restart.
- Ascension is the successful endgame, 4-phase cinematic (~22s) with philosophy-dependent endings (Shepherd's Rest / The Franchise / The Ascension). Credits include Wesley (Creative Direction), The Agent (Lead Design).

# BMF3K — QA DISCIPLINE

**Version:** 1.0  
**Status:** APPROVED — Derived from live codebase  
**Pillar:** 7 of 7 (QA Discipline)  
**Governance Phase:** 7 — Core Pillars Execution  
**Last Audit:** May 2026  

---

## 1. PURPOSE

This document defines the quality assurance standards, testing protocols, and regression prevention rules for BMF3K. It establishes what "shippable" means, what must be tested before any change is deployed, and how defects are classified and triaged.

**Rule:** No change ships without passing the QA checklist defined in this document.

---

## 2. QA PHILOSOPHY

BMF3K follows a **"Trust the Server, Verify the Client"** philosophy:

1. **Server is authoritative.** All game state mutations happen server-side. The client is a display layer.
2. **Client is suspect.** localStorage, client state, and DOM are convenience layers that can desync.
3. **Build must pass.** TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) and production build (`yarn build`) with zero errors.
4. **Budget must hold.** First-load JS must stay under **245KB**. Current baseline: ~162KB.
5. **Locked files stay locked.** `encounter.ts` (792 lines) is frozen. No modifications under any circumstances.

---

## 3. TESTING TIERS

BMF3K uses a 4-tier testing approach, from fastest to most thorough:

### Tier 1: Static Analysis (Automated, Every Change)

| Check | Tool | Pass Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Type safety | `tsc --noEmit` | Zero errors |
| Build integrity | `yarn build` | Successful production build |
| Bundle size | Build output | First Load JS ≤ 245KB |

**Frequency:** Every code change, before checkpoint.

### Tier 2: Smoke Test (Automated, Every Change)

| Check | Method | Pass Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Server starts | Dev server launch | Ready within 10s |
| Homepage loads | `curl localhost:3000` | HTTP 200, non-empty body |
| No console errors | Browser check | Zero unhandled exceptions |
| No 404/500 on load | Network inspection | All resources resolve |

**Frequency:** Every code change, after Tier 1 passes.

### Tier 3: Flow Verification (Manual, Feature Changes)

| Flow | Steps | Pass Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| New game | Menu → Character Creator → Hub | Player arrives at hub with correct stats |
| Mission dispatch | Hub → Clipboard → Select NPC → Dispatch | Mission appears in active list |
| Expedition cycle | Dispatch → Wait → Return → Resolution | Expedition resolves with narrative |
| NPC dosing | Hub → Dose Station → Select substance → Dose | Tolerance updates, reaction displays |
| Coffee brewing | Hub → Brewmatic → Select type → Brew | Stat increments, daily cap enforced |
| Day cycle | Hub → Sleep → Day-End Screen → Next Day | Day counter increments, resources consumed |
| Scrounge | Hub → Scrounge Station → Search | Resources found or narrative failure |
| Room navigation | Hub → Switch rooms → Verify ambience | Correct room renders, audio crossfades |

**Frequency:** When the related feature is modified.

### Tier 4: Regression Sweep (Manual, Major Changes)

Full playthrough from new game through at least 3 complete day cycles, verifying:

- All stations accessible and functional
- All hotkeys working
- Audio system responding correctly (music, ambience, SFX)
- Escalation system triggering at correct thresholds
- No hydration errors in console
- Mobile layout intact (viewport test at 375px width)
- Onboarding carousel displays on first visit
- Settings panel functional

**Frequency:** Before major deployments or after architectural changes.

---

## 4. DEFECT CLASSIFICATION

| Severity | Definition | Response Time | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0 — Blocker** | Game unplayable; data loss; build broken | Immediate fix before any other work | Build fails, API returns 500, session corruption |
| **P1 — Critical** | Major feature broken; workaround exists | Fix in current session | Dosing doesn't update tolerance, coffee ignores daily cap |
| **P2 — Major** | Feature partially broken; cosmetic impact | Fix in next session | Audio doesn't crossfade, stat chart misaligned |
| **P3 — Minor** | Cosmetic only; no functional impact | Backlog | Tooltip misaligned by 2px, colour slightly off |
| **P4 — Enhancement** | Not a bug; improvement suggestion | Backlog (requires governance review) | "Add a 5th coffee type" |

---

## 5. REGRESSION PREVENTION RULES

### 5.1 File Lock Policy

| File | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `encounter.ts` | 🔒 LOCKED (792 lines) | Core encounter engine, battle-tested, too risky to modify |
| `lib/game-data.ts` | ⚠️ CAREFUL | Contains all NPC data, mission definitions, constants |
| `lib/game-engine.ts` | ⚠️ CAREFUL | Core game logic, tolerance calculations |
| `api/game/encounter/route.ts` | ⚠️ CAREFUL | Encounter resolution, server-authoritative |

### 5.2 Empty Catch Blocks

Empty catch blocks (`catch {}` / `catch () {}`) are **intentional** throughout the codebase, particularly in:

- Audio initialisation (browser API failures are non-fatal)
- localStorage access (private browsing mode throws)
- Image preloading (network failures are non-fatal)

**Rule:** Do not add error logging to intentionally empty catch blocks. They are silent by design.

### 5.3 Server Authority Checks

Before any feature ships, verify:

1. Can the player cheat by modifying localStorage? → If yes, add server validation.
2. Can the player bypass a cap by rapid-clicking? → If yes, add button disable during API call.
3. Does the client optimistically update before server confirms? → If yes, ensure rollback on failure.

### 5.4 Bundle Size Gate

```
Current:   ~162KB first load
Ceiling:    245KB first load
Headroom:   ~83KB
```

Every new dependency must justify its size impact. Prefer:
- Dynamic imports (`next/dynamic`) for station components
- Web Audio API synthesis over audio files for SFX
- Inline SVG over icon libraries where possible
- Tree-shakeable imports (`import { X } from 'lucide-react'` not `import * as Icons`)

### 5.5 Hydration Safety

BMF3K suppresses hydration warnings via CSS (`[data-hydration-error] { display: none !important; }`). However, new components must still avoid hydration mismatches:

- No `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, or `new Date()` in render paths
- No `window` or `document` access outside `useEffect`
- No conditional rendering based on `localStorage` in initial render
- Use `useState` + `useEffect` pattern for client-only values

---

## 6. DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST

Before every deployment:

- [ ] `tsc --noEmit` passes (zero errors)
- [ ] `yarn build` succeeds
- [ ] First Load JS ≤ 245KB
- [ ] Dev server starts and serves HTTP 200
- [ ] No new console errors in browser
- [ ] encounter.ts unchanged (verify with `wc -l` = 792)
- [ ] All modified features manually smoke-tested
- [ ] Checkpoint created via `build_and_save_nextjs_project_checkpoint`
- [ ] Bundle size delta noted in checkpoint description

---

## 7. API HEALTH CHECKS

Every API endpoint must handle these cases:

| Case | Expected Response | HTTP Status |
|---|---|---|
| Missing sessionId | `{ error: 'Missing sessionId' }` | 400 |
| Invalid sessionId format | `{ error: 'Invalid sessionId' }` | 400 |
| Session not found | `{ error: 'Session not found' }` | 404 |
| Rate limit / daily cap exceeded | `{ error: 'already_used', message: '...' }` | 409 |
| Server error | `{ error: '...' }` | 500 |

All API routes use `isValidId()` from `lib/api-guards.ts` for input validation.

---

## 8. MOBILE QA STANDARDS

BMF3K is designed mobile-first. Mobile-specific checks:

| Check | Method | Pass Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Touch targets | Visual inspection | All buttons ≥ 44px touch target |
| Text readability | 375px viewport | All text ≥ 8px with `tracking-wider` |
| Scroll behaviour | Touch scroll test | No stuck scrolls, no bounce issues |
| Station layouts | 375px viewport | All stations usable without horizontal scroll |
| Audio on mobile | iOS Safari test | Audio initialises on first tap |

---

## 9. KNOWN ACCEPTABLE STATES

Some states appear broken but are intentional:

| State | Why It's Intentional |
|---|---|
| Interface degradation (glitching, colour shifts) | Escalation system — the game is reacting to player behaviour |
| Empty crew list on day 1 | Player hasn't recruited anyone yet |
| "COME BACK NEXT SHIFT" on coffee | Daily cap enforced — working as designed |
| Codex entries with redacted text | Narrative design — information is revealed progressively |
| Stat at 10 with coffee button greyed | Stat cap — cannot exceed 10 |

---

## 10. INCIDENT RESPONSE

When a player reports a bug:

1. **Check server logs first** — most issues leave traces in API error logs.
2. **Reproduce in dev** — use browser dev tools, network tab, console.
3. **Classify severity** — use the defect classification table (Section 4).
4. **Fix and verify** — for P0/P1, use browser automation to confirm the fix.
5. **Checkpoint** — always checkpoint after a fix.
6. **Document** — if the bug reveals a gap in this QA spec, update the spec.

---

## 11. GOVERNANCE INTEGRATION

This QA Discipline pillar interfaces with all other pillars:

| Pillar | QA Touchpoint |
|---|---|
| Pillar 1 (Core Loop) | Verify all mechanical rules are server-enforced |
| Pillar 2 (Navigation) | Verify all phase transitions are valid |
| Pillar 3 (Interactions) | Verify every interaction type follows its pattern |
| Pillar 5 (Audio) | Verify mute compliance, no hard cuts |

---

*End of Pillar 7 — QA Discipline*

# BMF3K — NAVIGATION PILLAR BRIEF

**Version:** 1.0  
**Status:** APPROVED — Derived from live codebase  
**Pillar:** 2 of 7 (Navigation & Flow)  
**Governance Phase:** 7 — Core Pillars Execution  
**Last Audit:** May 2026  

---

## 1. PURPOSE

This document defines every navigable state in BMF3K, the rules that govern transitions between them, and the gate conditions that lock or unlock access. It is the deterministic flow skeleton upon which all other pillars depend.

**Constraint:** If a phase transition is not listed here, it does not exist.

---

## 2. PHASE TAXONOMY

BMF3K operates on a strict phase system. The game client renders exactly one screen at a time based on the current phase. There are **28 discrete phases** organized into 7 functional groups.

### 2.1 Onboarding Sequence (6 phases)

| Phase | Screen | Purpose | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev_intro` | DevIntroScreen | Studio/engine ident | Auto-advance |
| `disclaimer` | DisclaimerScreen | Content warning + consent gate | User-click |
| `pipe_loading` | PipeLoadingScreen | Thematic loading animation | Auto-advance |
| `launch_intro` | LaunchIntroScreen | Narrative cold open | Auto-advance |
| `menu_transition` | MenuTransition | Visual bridge to menu | Auto-advance |
| `menu` | MainMenuScreen | Title screen + New/Continue | User-click |

**Flow:**
```
dev_intro → disclaimer → pipe_loading → launch_intro → menu_transition → menu
```

**Rules:**
- Sequence is linear and non-skippable on first play.
- `disclaimer` is a hard gate — requires explicit user consent click.
- No game state exists during onboarding. Session is created at `character_creator`.

### 2.2 Entry Sequence (2 phases)

| Phase | Screen | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `title_slideshow` | TitleSlideshow | Cinematic title card sequence |
| `character_creator` | CharacterCreator | 5-step Clinical History (stats + name + philosophy) |
| `character_sequence` | CharacterSequence | NPC introductions + pipe animation |

**New Game Flow:**
```
menu [NEW GAME] → character_creator → character_sequence → hub
```

**Continue Flow:**
```
menu [CONTINUE] → title_slideshow → welcome_back → hub
```

**Rules:**
- `character_creator` creates the DB session (GameSession + 4 NPCs + 4 resources + missions).
- `character_sequence` is a non-interactive cinematic. Player cannot skip individual phases within it.
- `title_slideshow` routes to EITHER `character_creator` (new) or `welcome_back` (load) via `postSlideshowPhase` state.

### 2.3 Hub (1 phase, 3 rooms)

The hub is a single phase (`hub`) containing 3 navigable rooms. Room transitions are lateral — they don't change the game phase.

| Room | Key | Stations | Theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operations Centre 1 | `ops_centre_1` | CREW BOARD, DISPATCH, SCAVENGE MAP, DOSE CONSOLE | Command & control |
| Operations Centre 2 | `ops_centre_2` | THE STASH, SCROUNGE | Resources & supply |
| Bedroom | `bedroom` | THE SHRINE, THE BOX, THE SHOEBOX | Personal / narrative |

**Room Navigation:**
- Keyboard: `7` = OPS 1, `8` = OPS 2, `9` = Bedroom
- Mobile: Swipe left/right
- Click: Room indicator bar at bottom of hub
- Default entry room: `ops_centre_1`

### 2.4 Station Phases (9 phases)

Each station is its own phase. Entering a station transitions from `hub` to the station phase. Exiting returns to `hub`.

| Station | Phase | Room | Hotkey | Transition Text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CREW BOARD | `clipboard` | OPS 1 | `1` | "ACCESSING PERSONNEL FILES..." |
| DISPATCH | `operations` | OPS 1 | `2` | "LOADING DIRECTIVES..." |
| SCAVENGE MAP | `map_table` | OPS 1 | `3` | "SCANNING PERIMETER..." |
| DOSE CONSOLE | `dosing` | OPS 1 | `4` | "INITIALIZING SUBSTANCE ADMIN..." |
| THE STASH | `inventory` | OPS 2 | `1` | "OPENING THE STASH..." |
| SCROUNGE | `scrounge` | OPS 2 | `2` | "CHECKING THE ALLEY..." |
| THE SHRINE | `hallucination` | Bedroom | `1` | "SITTING DOWN..." |
| THE BOX | `codex` | Bedroom | `2` | "LIFTING THE LID..." |
| THE SHOEBOX | `scrapbook` | Bedroom | `3` | "REACHING UNDER THE BED..." |

**Rules:**
- Station hotkeys (1-4) are contextual to the current room.
- `ESC` from any station phase returns to `hub`.
- Station entry plays a brief transition overlay (~800ms) before rendering station content.
- Exiting a station restores room-specific ambient music via `audioManager.restoreRoomMusic()`.

### 2.5 Action Phases (2 phases)

| Phase | Trigger | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `recruiting` | Click "RECRUIT" on unrecruited NPC in Crew Board | Completion → `hub`, Back → `hub` |
| `expedition` | Dispatch mission from Scavenge Map | Completion → `hub` |

**Recruitment Sub-Flow (3 stages, not separate phases):**
```
recruiting → [Stage 1: SURVEILLANCE] → [Stage 2: DISSECTION] → [Stage 3: THE PITCH] → hub
```
- Each stage is a component swap within the `recruiting` phase.
- Costs 1 energy per stage advancement.
- Completion sets `npc.recruited = true` and returns to `hub`.

**Expedition Sub-Flow:**
```
expedition → [Planning clipboard] → [Grid execution] → [Encounter system] → hub
```
- Costs 2 energy to dispatch.
- Encounters are resolved by `encounter.ts` (LOCKED — 792 lines, do not modify).
- Completion returns loot + heat to session and transitions to `hub`.

### 2.6 Day Lifecycle (4 phases)

| Phase | Screen | Trigger | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `night_cycle` | NightCycleScreen | Player presses `E` / END DAY or auto-triggers | Interactive (3-step ritual) |
| `night_blackout` | NightBlackoutScreen | Completes after night_cycle | Auto-advance (~3s) |
| `day_end` | DayEndScreen | Completes after night_blackout | User-click to continue |
| `welcome_back` | WelcomeBackScreen | After day advancement + load game | User-click to enter hub |

**Day End Flow:**
```
hub → [E key / END DAY] → night_cycle → [consume API fires] → night_blackout → day_end → [branch]
```

**Day End Branching:**
```
day_end → IF heat >= 10:     game_over (reason: heat)
        → IF heat >= 7:      raid check (deterministic pseudo-random)
          → IF raid triggers: raid → [survived?] → game_over OR advance day → hub
          → IF no raid:       advance day → hub
        → ELSE:              advance day → hub
```

**Night Cycle Save Ritual:**
The night cycle contains a 3-step interactive ritual:
1. **Nightlight** — Click to toggle on
2. **Lullaby** — Click to play tape
3. **Thumb** — Click to confirm sleep position

All 3 must be confirmed before the screen advances. Order is free but all are required.

### 2.7 End States (3 phases)

| Phase | Trigger | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `raid` | Heat ≥ 7 + deterministic roll at day_end | RaidScreen → survived / failed |
| `game_over` | Heat ≥ 10 OR failed raid | GameOverScreen → restart to menu |
| `ascension` | Complete "THE ASCENSION" mission (DIRECTIVE-OMEGA) | AscensionScreen → HUD strip → childhood bedroom |

**Raid Probability:**
```
IF heat >= 7:
  raidChance = (heat - 6) * 0.15
  roll = abs((day * 7 + 13) % 100) / 100  // deterministic, not random
  IF roll < raidChance: trigger raid
```

**Ascension Trigger:**
- Completing the `ascension` mission in OperationsBoard fires `onAscension()`.
- 2-second delay before phase transition.
- Ascension is the ONLY positive end state.

---

## 3. GATE CONDITIONS

Access to stations, content, and missions is gated by game state. All gates are evaluated client-side from server-authoritative data.

### 3.1 Station Gates

All 9 stations are available from Day 1. There are no station-level gates. The gating occurs within station *content*, not station *access*.

### 3.2 Codex Fragment Gates (12 fragments)

| Fragment | Gate Condition |
|---|---|
| Clinic Note (Dave) | Always available |
| Eviction Notice | Always available |
| Charity Flyer | Day ≥ 2 |
| Newspaper Clipping | Day ≥ 2 |
| Dave's Resignation | Dave recruited |
| Tamara's Prescription | Tamara recruited |
| Sid's Incident Report | Sid recruited |
| Mikey's Sermon Tape | Mikey recruited |
| Anonymous Note | Escalation ≥ 3 |
| Internal Memo (Coles) | Escalation ≥ 5 |
| Mother's Letter | Day ≥ 5 |
| Note in Your Handwriting | Escalation ≥ 7 |

### 3.3 Scrapbook Page Gates (10 pages)

| Page | Title | Gate Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | My Boy | Always available |
| 2 | The Fridge Door | Day ≥ 2 |
| 3 | The Report Card | Any NPC recruited |
| 4 | The Article | Day ≥ 5 |
| 5 | The Soup | Escalation ≥ 3 |
| 6 | The Tape | Day ≥ 4 |
| 7 | The Phone Bill | Escalation ≥ 5 |
| 8 | The Visit | Escalation ≥ 7 |
| 9 | The Letter | Day ≥ 5 |
| 10 | Come Home | Escalation ≥ 9 OR phase = ascension |

### 3.4 Shrine Memory Gates (8 base memories)

Shrine memories (THE BEDSIDE, THE PORTRAIT, THE TAPES, THE BOOK, THE JAR, THE BRUSH, HER THINGS, THE LIGHT) are all available from first shrine visit. Additional dynamic memories may scale with escalation via `allMemories` computation.

### 3.5 Mission Prerequisite Chain

```
[AVAILABLE from Day 1]
├── PARKING LOT SWEEP (Expedition, Tier 1) — no prereqs
├── FOOD COURT RAID (Expedition, Tier 1) — no prereqs
└── THE INITIATION (Main, Tier 1) — no prereqs
    └── Unlocks:
        ├── STORAGE CRAWL (Expedition, Tier 2)
        └── THE TERRITORY WAR (Main, Tier 2)
            └── Unlocks:
                ├── SECURITY BREACH (Expedition, Tier 3)
                └── THE SYNDICATE HANDSHAKE (Main, Tier 3)
                    └── Unlocks:
                        └── THE ASCENSION (Main, Tier 4) — ENDGAME
```

**Crew Requirements:**
- Tier 1: 1 recruited NPC
- Tier 2: 2 recruited NPCs
- Tier 3: 3 recruited NPCs
- Tier 4 (Ascension): 4 recruited NPCs (full crew)

---

## 4. GLOBAL NAVIGATION CONTROLS

| Input | Context | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `7` / `8` / `9` | Hub | Navigate to OPS 1 / OPS 2 / Bedroom |
| `1`–`4` | Hub (any room) | Open station by hotkey position |
| `E` | Hub | End day (→ night_cycle) |
| `S` | Hub | Sleep shortcut (→ night_cycle) |
| `T` | Hub | Toggle toolbar expansion |
| `ESC` | Station phase | Return to hub |
| `ESC` | Overlay open | Close overlay first |
| `M` | Global | Toggle mute |
| `?` | Global | Toggle hotkey overlay |
| Swipe L/R | Hub (mobile) | Navigate rooms |

---

## 5. AUDIO ROUTING BY PHASE

Phase determines ambient audio. Room within hub determines room-specific ambience.

| Phase Group | Audio |
|---|---|
| Menu + Onboarding | Menu theme (plays once) |
| Hub (OPS rooms) | Hub ambience + menu theme in "radio mode" (lowpass filter) |
| Hub (Bedroom) | Dual candle glow atmosphere, near-silence |
| Stations (OPS) | Station-specific ambience (inventory jingle, etc.) |
| Shrine | Near-silence + voice clip on hotspot interaction |
| Scrapbook | Clock tick (800Hz sine) + fridge hum (60Hz + harmonic) |
| Recruitment | Phase-specific Web Audio synthesis |
| Expedition | Expedition ambience + voice clips |
| Night Cycle | Silence (ritual focus) |
| Game Over | Denied SFX + thud |
| Ascension | Progressive silence as HUD strips away |

---

## 6. VIGNETTE INTENSITY BY PHASE

The screen vignette (dark edge overlay) scales with phase context:

| Phase Context | Vignette Opacity |
|---|---|
| Hub | 0.5 |
| Stations (OPS) | 0.6 |
| Shrine, Night Cycle, Blackout, Raid, Game Over | 0.9 |
| Default | 0.5 |

---

## 7. COMPLETE FLOW DIAGRAM

```

Bum-a-Fag / BMF 3000 Feature Expansion Production Spec

## Overview

This document defines the next production phase for **Bum-a-Fag / BMF 3000** as an expansion of an existing game rather than a from-scratch build.[cite:1] The scope of this phase is to integrate a node-based travel layer, passive travel events, travel-specific combat encounters, and a finalized socket-based dice combat loop with a stacking spiritual attack meter and a lighter-charged special move.[cite:82][cite:45][cite:113]

The goal of this phase is to make travel feel physical and atmospheric, deepen the combat system, and unify these features with the gameâ€™s existing year-3000-allegedly tone and lighter/glass visual language.[cite:3][cite:2][cite:4][cite:119]

## Production framing

This phase should be treated as a **feature expansion and systems pass** on an already existing project, not as initial implementation of the whole game.[cite:1] Internal planning, prompts, and implementation notes should describe the work as adding or integrating new systems into the current build so downstream agents or collaborators do not misread the project as a greenfield game build.[cite:1][cite:82]

Core framing for this phase:

- Existing project: Bum-a-Fag / BMF 3000.[cite:1]
- New work is additive: travel map, event layer, combat refinement, and spiritual attack implementation.[cite:82]
- The output of this phase is a working feature-complete vertical slice of those additions, not a full rebuild.[cite:82]

## Scope

This phase includes four connected systems:[cite:82]

- Node-based travel map and travel transition UI.[cite:45][cite:113]
- Passive travel event system with weighted outcomes.[cite:112]
- Travel-combat encounter layer using the existing socket-dice concept.[cite:82][cite:115]
- Spiritual attack meter, charge sequence, and first power attack implementation.[cite:82][cite:119]

This phase does not require rebuilding the gameâ€™s existing core structure, story base, or previously completed content.[cite:1][cite:3]

## Design goals

- Replace instant location switching with travel that feels embodied and legible through a visual route transition.[cite:45][cite:113]
- Add atmosphere and pacing during movement without turning travel into a second main game mode.[cite:112][cite:122]
- Keep the game hard but avoid overpunishing travel through excessive attrition.[cite:82]
- Make combat tactical through dice allocation choices rather than raw randomness alone.[cite:115][cite:70]
- Give the special slot a long-term strategic purpose through a stacking meter and payoff attack.[cite:82][cite:119]
- Maintain tonal consistency with the gameâ€™s dirty, delusional, allegedly futuristic worldbuilding.[cite:3][cite:2][cite:4]

## Travel map system

### System summary

Travel should use a **node-based map overlay** connecting existing areas rather than free-roam movement.[cite:45][cite:113][cite:122] The player remains area-based, but movement between areas is now visualized through route selection and a brief animated transition.[cite:45]

### Intended player flow

1. Player is in an area screen.
2. Player selects **Travel**.
3. Travel map overlay opens over the current play context.[cite:45]
4. Player selects a connected destination node.[cite:113]
5. UI shows route cost, travel time, and any route tags.
6. Travel animation plays with moving character marker on dotted route.
7. Optional passive event may trigger during the journey.
8. Player arrives in destination area and area state loads.

### Travel map UI

Required UI elements:

- Static stylized area map background.
- Visible travel nodes for reachable areas.[cite:113]
- Route lines between nodes, ideally dotted or segmented.[cite:45]
- Current location highlight.
- Locked node state for progression-gated areas.[cite:112]
- Destination card showing area name, route cost, route time, and risk/flavor tags.
- Moving face/head/icon representing the player during transit.

### Travel animation

Travel animation should be brief, readable, and atmospheric rather than cinematic.[cite:45] The marker moves along a visible route while the path highlights or pulses beneath it.[cite:45]

Recommended animation beats:

- Route line activates.
- Character marker moves along path.
- Ambient text or status beat appears if an event is triggered.
- Arrival pause before loading destination.

Recommended duration: 1 to 3 seconds for standard travel, longer only when an event interrupts the journey.[cite:45]

### Initial implementation target

- 6 travel nodes total.
- 2 to 4 outbound links per node.
- 2 to 3 locked nodes tied to progression.
- Route metadata for time, cost, and event weighting.

## Travel event system

### System summary

Travel events are lightweight route incidents that fire during movement.[cite:112] They are not full side missions and should not derail the destination-focused structure of the map system.[cite:122]

### Design role

Travel events should do three jobs:

- Add world texture and street-level grime.
- Nudge resources and pacing.
- Foreshadow the destination or mission state.[cite:3]

### Event pool size

Target pool: **30 total travel events**.

Planned split:

| Event type | Count | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Resource events | 12 | 40% |
| Character/dialogue events | 12 | 40% |
| Combat events | 6 | 20% |

This keeps resource events as the biggest category while preserving enough space for voiced weirdos and occasional danger.[cite:82]

### Trigger model

- Roll once per trip in most cases.
- Trigger chance should be moderate rather than constant.
- Long routes may support a second roll later if balancing supports it.
- Events should be weighted by route, time, story state, and possibly weather or area condition if those systems exist.

### Event data structure

Recommended event schema:

- `id`
- `type` (resource, character, combat)
- `eligibleRoutes`
- `eligibleNodes`
- `conditions`
- `weight`
- `once`
- `cooldown`
- `dialogue`
- `effect`
- `followupState`

## Resource events

### Rules

Resource events should be the most common and the least punishing category.[cite:82] Losses should generally remove only **1 unit** of a resource, while gains should usually award **2 units** of something.[cite:82]

### Resource event targets

Candidate resource types:

- Cigarettes.
- Cash.
- Scrap butts or loose tobacco.
- Lighter fuel or lighter charge.
- Time.
- Morale, composure, or similar soft state.

### Jackpot events

Include **1 or 2 jackpot resource events** in the entire pool with very low weight.[cite:82] These should feel rare and memorable rather than farmable.[cite:112]

## Character events

### Rules

Character events are mostly short worldbuilding beats delivered as one or two lines of dialogue.[cite:3] They are ideal for custom voice lines and should lean into strange year-3000 social texture.[cite:3]

### Character event functions

- Introduce quirky future street characters.
- Deliver overheard rumors.
- Humiliate or unsettle the player socially.
- Foreshadow the next areaâ€™s mood or mission context.
- Reinforce the gameâ€™s spiritual/delusional tone.[cite:3]

### Tone examples

Character beats should feel like failed futurism mixed with damaged street myth: tram prophets, nicotine monks, synthetic beggars, dead-eyed transit zealots, broken machine philosophers, and other oddballs who feel plausible inside the existing world.[cite:3]

## Travel combat encounters

### Rules

Combat events on the travel map should be uncommon and short.[cite:82] They should feel like ugly interruptions rather than standard mission scenes.

### Design target

- Low HP.
- 1 to 3 rounds where possible.
- Fast resolution.
- Small loot or survival-based reward.
- Moderate attrition, not massive punishment.[cite:82]

### Encounter archetypes

Initial enemy archetype list:

- Mugger or scavenger.
- Rival bum.
- Security-type threat.
- Future-preacher or spiritual loon.
- Opportunist thief.
- Glass-weapon psycho.

## Combat system

### Core model

Combat uses a **socket-based 3d6 allocation system** already defined for the project.[cite:82] At the start of each round, the player rolls 3 free d6 and assigns them across Attack, Defense, and Special sockets.[cite:82]

### Socket rules

| Socket | Dice limit | Function |
|---|---:|---|
| Attack | 2 | Builds attack total |
| Defense | 2 | Builds defense total |
| Special | 1 | Adds meter / triggers special state |

The player chooses how aggressively or defensively to distribute the roundâ€™s dice, creating tactical tradeoffs each turn.[cite:82][cite:115]

### Resolution rules

- Player Attack total is compared with enemy Defense total.[cite:82]
- Enemy Attack total is compared with player Defense total.[cite:82]
- If Attack is higher than Defense, the attack lands.[cite:82]
- If Attack is equal to or lower than Defense, no damage is dealt.[cite:82]

### Damage model

For this phase, damage should primarily come from **base build strength**, weapon values, or other character stats rather than from raw die faces alone.[cite:82][cite:103][cite:105] Dice should decide who wins the exchange; stats and gear should decide how much that success hurts.[cite:99][cite:103]

Recommended damage formula for initial balancing:

- Successful hit = base weapon damage + strength modifier.
- Optional margin bonus = +1 damage or small rider effect if attack exceeds defense by a notable amount.
- Keep modifiers small and readable.

This split preserves tactical allocation while making progression and equipment meaningful.[cite:103][cite:105]

## Spiritual attack system

### Meter rules

The Special socket feeds a **Spiritual Attack meter** that persists across turns until it reaches 12.[cite:82] Each die placed into Special adds its face value to the meter.[cite:82]

When the meter reaches **12 or more**, the player becomes able to trigger a spiritual attack sequence.[cite:82][cite:119] This makes Special a long-term investment rather than a simple immediate buff.[cite:119]

### Charged state

Once charged:

- UI should clearly show that the spiritual attack is ready.
- The next use of the Special socket should initiate the power attack sequence rather than only adding more meter.
- Post-use reset behavior still needs final balancing; recommended initial rule is full reset or partial reset to a low carryover value.

### Visual language

This system should align with the projectâ€™s established lighter, smoke, and bulb-ended glass object imagery.[cite:2][cite:4][cite:82] The spiritual attack is not polished sci-fi magic; it should feel ritualistic, dirty, physical, and improvised.[cite:3][cite:82]

## Spiritual attack interaction

### First special move

The first implemented spiritual attack uses a small bulb-ended glass weapon.[cite:82] On activation:

1. The weapon rises into frame.[cite:82]
2. The player applies a lighter flame to the bulb.[cite:82]
3. Holding the flame charges the attack.[cite:82]
4. Charged release unleashes the special move.[cite:82]

### Minigame structure

Recommended implementation:

- Short hold-to-charge interaction.
- Charge duration around 1 to 2 seconds.[cite:89][cite:92]
- Clear audiovisual feedback during charge.
- Optional sweet spot or full-charge threshold.
- Keep interaction short enough to remain satisfying over repeated use.[cite:89]

### Result

Best first implementation outcome:

- Heavy damage.
- Ignores defense.
- Strong bespoke visual and sound payoff.

Optional later expansions can add stagger, armor break, meter drain, or multi-target variants.

## Enemy design

### Design approach

Enemy identity should come primarily from **socket behavior and combat priorities**, not huge stat sheets.[cite:115] This reduces design load while preserving combat variety.

### Initial archetypes

| Archetype | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Rusher | Heavy Attack investment, weak Defense |
| Coward | High Defense, weak finishing power |
| Trickster | Frequent Special usage, disruptive effects |
| Tank | Stable Defense with moderate Attack |
| Glass psycho | Big Attack spikes, low survivability |
| Opportunist | Balanced until player is weak, then aggressive |

## UI and UX requirements

### Travel UI

- Overlay-based map presentation rather than full hard-cut menu.[cite:45]
- Clear current-node and reachable-node state.[cite:113]
- Route preview with time/cost values.
- Dotted route animation.
- Moving face or head icon.
- Mid-route event card overlay when an event fires.

### Combat UI

- Three rolled dice displayed prominently each round.
- Clear socket destinations for Attack, Defense, and Special.
- Drag or tap assignment interaction.
- Live totals or clear slot values.
- Visible spiritual meter from 0 to 12.[cite:82]
- Clear â€œchargedâ€ state feedback when special is ready.[cite:82]

### Special attack UI

- Distinct transition into the lighter-charge sequence.[cite:82]
- Bespoke visuals matching existing project motifs of flame, smoke, and glass.[cite:2][cite:4][cite:82]
- Fast return into combat resolution after the move executes.

## Narrative and tone alignment

The added systems must match the existing tone of BMF 3000 rather than reading like generic RPG features.[cite:1][cite:3] The year-3000 framing is unstable and possibly delusional, and the gameâ€™s fiction already leans on smoke, fire, damaged spirituality, and weird ritual energy.[cite:3][cite:2][cite:4]

Travel events, enemy archetypes, UI feedback, and spiritual attacks should all reinforce that same identity.[cite:3][cite:82]

## Implementation order

Recommended production order:

1. Lock resource list and any soft-state variables.
2. Finalize the 6-node travel layout and route graph.
3. Implement travel overlay UI and dotted-route movement.
4. Add event schema and weighted event triggering.
5. Write and integrate the 30-event pool.
6. Formalize combat calculations around sockets and base-damage model.
7. Implement the visible spiritual meter and charged state.
8. Build the first lighter-charge special sequence.
9. Add the first 6 travel-combat enemy archetypes.
10. Balance encounter frequency, damage output, and travel attrition.
11. Add voice lines, VFX, and polish.

## Minimum viable deliverable for this phase

A successful delivery for this phase should include:

- One working travel map overlay.
- Six connected travel nodes.
- Animated route movement.
- Thirty weighted travel events.
- Six travel-combat archetypes.
- Finalized round structure for the socket-dice combat system.[cite:82]
- Spiritual meter to 12 with charged state.[cite:82]
- One complete lighter-charged spiritual attack.[cite:82]
- Arrival-state integration with destination area loading.

## Open decisions

These items still require explicit final decisions during implementation:

- Exact resource list.
- Exact base-damage formula.
- Whether spiritual meter overflow carries over above 12.
- Whether failed spiritual charge resets meter fully or partially.
- Final event trigger rate.
- Whether certain weapons, traits, or builds alter socket rules.
- Whether time, weather, or mission state influence travel event pools at launch.

## Working principle

This feature phase should preserve a clear role for each system:

- Travel adds atmosphere and pacing.[cite:45][cite:112]
- Events add flavor, attrition, and foreshadowing.[cite:112][cite:3]
- Dice sockets create tactical pressure.[cite:82][cite:115]
- Base stats and gear define damage identity.[cite:103][cite:105]
- Spiritual charge creates delayed payoff and spectacle.[cite:82][cite:119]
- Tone is carried by the gameâ€™s broken year-3000 world and recurring lighter/glass/spiritual imagery.[cite:3]

# BMF:3K — Interactive Pitch Handover

**Working document · Structure, visual system, interaction rules, and implementation handover**

> Vibe check passed. Let's build.

## 0. Purpose

This document hands over the current structure for the **BMF:3K interactive pitch** before the next prototype build.

The pitch is not a conventional website with a science-fiction skin. It is a **living operational file**: the audience enters through a constructed 3K Overlay system, then explores BMF:3K through a persistent interface where visual evidence, the central hero proposition, and narrative documentation occupy distinct but connected zones.

This document is the current structural source of truth for the next prototype pass.

## 1. Project Identity

| Field | Decision |
|---|---|
| Project | BMF:3K |
| Position | Part II of the BMFU trilogy, pitched as a standalone |
| Format | Interactive pitch deck / exploratory narrative file |
| Tone | Bone-dry realism, dark comedy, psychological precision |
| Visual language | Analog operational dossier with a restrained 3K Overlay |
| Core thesis | Unmanaged reality is lethal. The systems we build to survive our wounds eventually become the wounds themselves. |
| Intro prompt | `MANAGE DECLINE` |
| AI attribution | Never include attribution such as “Prepared by: Manus AI” |
| Supernatural material | None; all phenomena remain chemically or psychologically sourced |
| Character framing | No villain framing; horror arises from sincerity and survival mechanisms |

## 2. Core Experience Statement

> **The opening builds the system. The hero page reveals what the system is managing.**

The audience should feel that they are entering a file which is actively registering, sorting, and containing the material of the film.

The 3K Overlay is therefore not decoration. It controls:

- framing
- spatial rhythm
- page transitions
- visual emphasis
- monitor-scan behaviour
- the relationship between art, hero content, and documentation

The narrative remains the substance. The Overlay is the perceptual grammar around it.

## 3. Experience Architecture

### 3.1 Launch state

The application opens into a dedicated 3K launch sequence.

The launch sequence:

- plays once on app launch
- lasts at least 6 seconds and no more than 9 seconds before the pitch is accessible
- constructs the Overlay rather than simply fading it in
- uses art-monitor scan language to reveal the entry prompt
- resolves to `> MANAGE DECLINE_`
- transitions into the main hero page
- does not replay during ordinary navigation

### 3.2 Post-launch state

After launch, the Overlay nests into the application shell.

It remains visible on every screen, but its intensity changes by page:

- **Main intro / hero page:** heavy Overlay treatment
- **All other tabs:** restrained but constant Overlay presence
- **Every screen:** slight page-specific rearrangement or variation

The system should feel continuous. Navigation should not feel like opening separate web pages.

### 3.3 Main shell

The pitch uses a three-zone composition:

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     3K OVERLAY FRAME                         │
├───────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────┤
│                   │                          │               │
│   ART / VISUALS   │       CENTRE HERO        │  NARRATIVE /  │
│                   │                          │     DOCS       │
│   image language  │   current page identity  │               │
│   Overlay traces  │   primary statement      │   copy         │
│   monitor scans   │   page-specific action   │   context      │
│   visual evidence │   main proposition       │   source notes │
│                   │                          │               │
├───────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────────────┤
│                 TAB / FILE NAVIGATION                         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 4. Launch Sequence — “Boot”

### 4.1 Timing contract

| Time | Beat | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–0.8s | Void | Black frame. Silence. No logo or visible grid. |
| 0.8–2.5s | Grid construction | Lime hairline grid traces itself into existence. Horizontal lines first, then vertical lines. |
| 2.5–3.3s | Diagnostic pass | A restrained magenta scan or trace passes across the completed field. |
| 3.3–5.5s | Monitor reveal | A horizontal monitor band sweeps downward, revealing the central title/status material through a mask or clipped scan. |
| 5.5–6.5s | Status resolve | Small status text settles with minimal flicker. |
| 6.5–8.5s | Entry prompt | `> MANAGE DECLINE_` appears with a blinking cursor. |
| 8.5–9.0s | Access boundary | The user can enter the pitch. The hard maximum is 9 seconds. |

### 4.2 Launch copy

Primary prompt:

```text
> MANAGE DECLINE_
```

The prompt is text-led and terminal-like. It should not look like a conventional rounded CTA button.

Supporting status copy may remain minimal and file-like, for example:

```text
FILE STATUS — STANDALONE / PART II OF III
```

Any supporting line must remain subordinate to the title and prompt.

### 4.3 Launch interaction rules

- The sequence must not block access beyond the 9-second maximum.
- The prompt becomes interactive once the minimum 6-second floor has passed.
- Click, tap, and keyboard Enter should provide access after the interaction boundary.
- The sequence plays once on app launch.
- Returning to the main page does not replay the boot sequence.
- The resolved Overlay state remains alive after the boot has ended.

### 4.4 Reduced-motion behaviour

If reduced motion is enabled:

- preserve the timing and order of the launch beats
- replace line-drawing with quick resolved line placement
- remove or reduce flicker
- replace the scan sweep with a controlled reveal
- retain the prompt and access boundary

## 5. Persistent 3K Overlay System

### 5.1 Two-layer model

The Overlay is divided into two related layers.

#### The Frame

The Frame is the persistent outer structure:

- top and bottom rules
- corner brackets
- side rails or registration marks
- page references and small ticks
- restrained accent changes

The Frame is always present after launch.

#### The Field

The Field is the interior grid and trace system:

- hairline geometry
- scan traces
- page-specific partitions
- controlled gaps or dropouts
- subtle colour and tempo changes

The Field is strongest on the launch and main hero page, then recedes on document-led pages.

### 5.2 Intensity tiers

| Tier | Location | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Tier A — Full Theme | Launch sequence and main hero / entry page | Strongest grid, active scan behaviour, visible corner brackets, full Overlay composition, highest visual confidence |
| Tier B — Nested Theme | All other tabs | Constant Frame, lower-opacity Field, slower and quieter changes, minimal interference with reading |

The design rule is:

> **The Overlay is loudest where the pitch is being felt, quieter where the pitch is being read.**

### 5.3 Colour discipline

The Overlay uses a restrained palette:

- black or near-black ground
- lime hairline traces
- magenta diagnostic accents
- occasional clinical blue where a page-specific variation calls for it

The Overlay must never become a literal sci-fi HUD. It remains perceptual, sparse, and materially connected to art-monitor and operational-file language.

## 6. Three-Zone Main Layout

### 6.1 Left zone — Art and visual evidence

The left side carries the visual language of the film.

It may contain:

- art-monitor textures
- scanned fragments
- restrained Overlay traces
- diagrams and measured marks
- objects, silhouettes, or visual motifs
- image-led reveals
- page-specific visual arrangements

This is not a decorative sidebar. It is the film’s visual memory.

Rules:

- visual material must earn its place
- it should change slightly per screen
- it can be more expressive than the documentation rail
- it must not compete with the central hero proposition
- the Overlay may frame or register the visual material without turning it into a dashboard

### 6.2 Centre zone — Hero page

The centre is the dominant visual and narrative anchor.

It contains:

- current page identity
- central title or proposition
- primary dramatic statement
- strongest page-specific visual composition
- one clear next action or route
- the most noticeable Overlay rearrangement

The centre is not a generic dashboard column. Each screen should use it to make a distinct argument about BMF:3K.

The main intro / hero page receives the heaviest 3K treatment.

### 6.3 Right zone — Narrative and documents

The right side is the reading and evidence layer.

It contains relevant material such as:

- narrative explanation
- character and story information
- production notes
- development documentation
- controlled trilogy context
- expandable supporting detail

Rules:

- typography and hierarchy take priority over visual effects
- the Overlay remains present but quiet
- long-form copy must remain readable
- scan marks, corner references, and small registration ticks are acceptable
- the right rail should feel like a document being examined, not a marketing card wall

## 7. Main Hero Page

The user enters the main hero page immediately after the launch sequence.

The page should include:

- `MANAGE DECLINE` as the resolved title
- a concise standalone BMF:3K premise
- the core dramatic proposition
- an immediate route into the pitch tabs
- left-side visual evidence
- right-side orientation and file context
- the strongest nested Overlay state

The hero page is the bridge between the constructed launch system and the narrative file.

It should answer, quickly and clearly:

1. What is this?
2. What is the pressure inside it?
3. Where can I go next?

## 8. Navigation and Page Families

The working pitch architecture contains eight primary areas:

1. Entry / Main Hero
2. Story
3. Household
4. System
5. Descent
6. The Big One
7. Why It Lands
8. Development

The navigation should be persistent but visually integrated into the file frame rather than presented as a generic SaaS tab bar.

### 8.1 Page behaviour matrix

| Page | Content emphasis | Overlay variation | Intensity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry / Main Hero | Central premise and orientation | Full resolved grid, active frame, strongest trace language | Tier A |
| Story | Narrative structure and dramatic movement | Standard grid with gentle pulse | Tier B |
| Household | Domestic pressure and contained space | Subtle vertical partitions suggesting rooms or zones | Tier B |
| System | The systems and mechanisms at work | Controlled hue cycling across the reference field | Tier B, with slightly higher visual activity |
| Descent | Deterioration and loss of control | Cells or traces drop out, creating controlled decay | Tier B |
| The Big One | Major dramatic pressure point | Faster tempo and tighter spacing | Tier B, with a sharper pulse |
| Why It Lands | The reason the material connects | Looser spacing and restrained clinical blue | Tier B, quietest release |
| Development | Production, framework, and controlled trilogy context | Standard field with an additional case-file tick or marker | Tier B |

These variations must remain minor. The user should always recognise the same operating system.

## 9. Page Transition Rules

Every navigation change should feel like the same file being re-read.

Transition sequence:

1. Centre hero shifts or re-registers.
2. Left visual field changes arrangement.
3. Right documentation column updates.
4. Overlay Frame briefly tightens or repositions.
5. Field settles into the selected page variation.

Target transition feel:

- restrained
- approximately 300–500ms where motion is used
- no hard reset of the whole interface
- no unrelated page theme
- no excessive ambient animation

Reduced-motion behaviour should use immediate or near-immediate state changes while preserving hierarchy and page identity.

## 10. Content and Canon Rules

The **BMF:3K — PITCH MASTER** remains the authority for narrative and canon.

The interactive pitch must preserve the following rules:

- BMF:3K remains the primary pitch.
- C1:V1 and Y2K:Finale appear only as controlled, vague, spoiler-free trilogy teases.
- The standalone nature of BMF:3K must remain clear.
- No AI attribution appears anywhere in the pitch.
- Do not introduce supernatural explanations.
- Do not frame characters as villains.
- Do not add unsupported story facts, production claims, figures, or achievements.
- Open decisions remain open until explicitly ruled on.

Known open narrative decisions from the pitch master remain separate from the interface structure:

- Casket Kiss
- final format confirmation
- prison timeline

The prototype must not silently resolve these.

## 11. Interaction Requirements

### Required

- launch sequence plays once on app launch
- access is available between 6 and 9 seconds
- `> MANAGE DECLINE_` is the launch prompt
- Enter key supports access after the interaction boundary
- main hero page loads after launch
- all primary tabs are navigable
- the Overlay remains visible on every page
- each page has a slight Overlay variation
- left, centre, and right zones are visually distinct
- navigation updates content rather than acting as decorative controls
- mobile layout collapses cleanly into a readable one-column sequence
- reduced-motion behaviour is supported
- focus-visible states are present for keyboard users

### Avoid

- replaying the boot on every tab change
- heavy animated noise behind long-form copy
- generic rounded SaaS cards
- a literal sci-fi HUD
- excessive neon or cyberpunk styling
- visual effects that obscure narrative text
- dead buttons or decorative tabs
- fake loading states
- unsupported canon or invented documentation

## 12. Responsive Structure

### Desktop

Use the full three-zone composition:

- left: art and visual evidence
- centre: hero proposition
- right: narrative and documents

The centre must remain visually dominant.

### Tablet

Maintain the hierarchy while narrowing the rails:

- centre remains primary
- left and right zones remain visible where space permits
- copy measure stays controlled
- Overlay intensity may reduce slightly to protect legibility

### Mobile

Collapse into a deliberate vertical sequence:

1. persistent top Frame / page reference
2. centre hero content
3. left visual evidence
4. right narrative and documents
5. navigation controls

The layout must not rely on horizontal overflow or tiny text. The Overlay should remain visible through corner marks, hairlines, and sparse traces rather than dense background geometry.

## 13. Visual Direction

### Direction

Analog operational dossier with art-monitor interference and psychological pressure.

### Palette

- near-black ground
- off-white document text
- lime structural traces
- magenta diagnostic accents
- restrained clinical blue on the release / thesis-oriented page

### Shape language

- sharp corners
- hairline rules
- registration marks
- brackets
- measured spacing
- no soft card-heavy treatment

### Typography

Use a technical geometric sans for interface labels and a restrained editorial display face only where the hero requires additional dramatic weight.

Recommended pairing for the prototype:

- interface / labels: Space Grotesk
- hero display: Fraunces used sparingly

All small labels should share one consistent uppercase, tracked label treatment.

### Motion

Motion is limited to a few purposeful behaviours:

1. launch grid construction and monitor reveal
2. one restrained page-transition rearrangement
3. small page-specific Overlay adjustments

No constant decorative animation should run behind reading material.

## 14. Prototype Scope

The next prototype pass should demonstrate the structure, not attempt to finalise every film asset.

### Must demonstrate

- launch sequence timing and prompt
- one-time launch behaviour
- main hero page after launch
- three-zone composition
- persistent nested Overlay
- at least four visibly distinct but restrained page variations
- navigation across all eight page labels
- right-side narrative/document content
- left-side visual evidence treatment
- responsive collapse
- reduced-motion fallback

### Can remain provisional

- final art assets
- final copy length
- exact page-specific imagery
- final case-file references
- final open-decision wording

Provisional material must be visibly treated as draft content in the development process, not presented as locked canon.
